comments.author: @StewartKayla-z3m
comments.text: Just finished threshing our teff crop under the shadow of the Simien Mountains and sat down with a hot cup of Jabena coffee to watch this! Living up here at high altitude means farming on steep, ancient soil that requires real endurance. Outsiders always get surprised that we eat sour Injera bread three times a day using zero cutlery, but it’s what keeps our community strong. How would you handle living in a place with a completely different calendar and clock system from the rest of the world? 🇪🇹

replies.author: @HappyTravel99
replies.text: What an incredible glimpse into daily life there. Farming teff beneath the Simien Mountains, sharing injera, and sitting down with Jabena coffee sounds like such a meaningful rhythm of life. As for the calendar and clock system, I think it would definitely take some adjustment at first, but that is also part of what makes Ethiopia so fascinating. Thank you for sharing a real local perspective with us — it adds so much to the conversation. 🇪🇹

comments.text: If you could spend one month anywhere in Ethiopia, would you choose the highlands, Addis Ababa, or a remote rural community?

replies.author: @HappyTravel99
replies.text: That’s a tough choice, but I’d probably choose the highlands. The landscapes, ancient history, traditional villages, and cooler climate would make a month there unforgettable. But Addis Ababa would be fascinating too for the food, culture, and everyday city life.

comments.text: Loved the documentary overall! Though I wish you had spent a bit more time explaining how our 13-month calendar and 7-year time difference actually work in daily life for tourists. Still, seeing the warmth of our people captured so authentically makes me proud. Drop your questions below if you're curious about visiting

replies.author: @HappyTravel99
replies.text: Thank you so much for the thoughtful feedback! We’re really glad the documentary made you feel proud, especially seeing the warmth and hospitality of Ethiopian people reflected in the video. You’re absolutely right that the 13-month calendar and the 7-year difference are fascinating parts of daily life and deserve more explanation. We’ll keep that in mind for future videos. And thank you for inviting others to ask questions about visiting Ethiopia — that kind of local perspective is incredibly valuable. ❤️🇪🇹

comments.author: @travellives
comments.text: Wait, so Ethiopia is currently 7–8 years behind the rest of us AND running on 13 months?!

replies.author: @HappyTravel99
replies.text: Yes — it sounds unbelievable at first! 😄 Ethiopia uses its own calendar with 13 months, and its year number is usually about 7–8 years behind the Gregorian calendar used in most of the world. It’s one of the many fascinating things that makes Ethiopia so unique. Thanks for watching! 🇪🇹☕
